data.description:
## Incident Overview

When the user explicitly tells the agent to run `/dso:fix-bug` (e.g., 'Use /fix-bug to diagnose this issue'), this constitutes direct human authorization — the user IS the intent signal. The CLI_user tag should be applied automatically and the intent-search gate should be skipped.

**Current behavior**: /dso:fix-bug dispatches the intent-search sub-agent even when the user explicitly invoked the skill in conversation.

**Expected behavior**: Explicit user invocation directive sets CLI_user tag on the bug ticket and skips the intent gate (equivalent to CLI_user pre-check path in Phase B Step 1).

**Why**: The CLI_user tag already has special semantics in fix-bug Phase B Step 1: 'If present, the intent is known and the intent-search agent can be skipped entirely.' A user saying 'use /fix-bug to resolve X' is the same signal. The intent gate exists to catch autonomous bug investigations that might be chasing a non-bug; it is unnecessary overhead when the user explicitly directs the investigation.
data.title: [fix-bug skill]: Explicit user invocation directive does not set CLI_user tag -> unnecessary intent-search dispatch
